classification.difficultyReason: Identify labelled bucket positions for two specified colours; the remaining positions must supply green toys.

content.prompt: Twelve labelled buckets each contain one red toy, one blue toy and one green toy. From each bucket, choose exactly one toy. In how many ways can four red toys and five blue toys be obtained?

answer.short:
$27\,720$

Choose four red bucket positions, then five blue positions from the remaining eight.
answer.worked:
Choose four of the twelve buckets to supply red toys, then five of the remaining eight to supply blue toys. The last three buckets must supply green toys.

$$\begin{align*}N&=\binom{12}{4}\binom{8}{5}\binom{3}{3}\\N&=495\times56\times1\\N&=27\,720.\end{align*}$$
